;Armed attacks and conflicts
*[[Khartoum massacre]]
**The Central Committee of Sudanese Doctors say the number of people killed this week in Sudan is at least 100, and that 40 bodies were pulled from the [[Nile|River Nile]] at [[Khartoum]] on Tuesday. Members of the [[Rapid Support Forces (Sudan)|Rapid Support Forces]] have reportedly been roaming the streets attacking civilians as it pushes deeper into Khartoum. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-48512413 (BBC News)]
**A Sudanese official denies that  100 people were killed by a paramilitary unit during protests, saying that the number was at most 46. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-48535165 (BBC News)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Russian involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**Syrian government and Russian warplanes conduct airstrikes that target Syria's northwest, killing five civilians in the town of Kansafra and three villages in Idlib, including two children. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/06/syrian-air-strikes-kill-civilians-besieged-idlib-190606070809591.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Government forces shell the northern Hama countryside, killing one civilian. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/06/syrian-air-strikes-kill-civilians-besieged-idlib-190606070809591.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Government air attacks hit a motorcycle in the Idlib town of Maaret al-Numan, killing a woman and her two children. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/06/syrian-air-strikes-kill-civilians-besieged-idlib-190606070809591.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Business and economy
*[[Fiat Chrysler Automobiles|Fiat Chrysler]] withdraws its merger proposal for French carmaker [[Renault]] after  Renault board members were unable to reach a decision on the offer. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-48537453 (BBC News)]
*[[YouTube]] announces a new policy regarding [[hate speech]] and harassment on the video sharing platform, saying it will specifically ban videos that include [[Neo-Nazism|neo-nazi]] and supremacist content, subsequently suspending several popular [[right-wing]] channels, and demonetizing [[Steven Crowder]]'s. [https://www.cnet.com/news/youtube-to-ban-supremacist-and-hoax-videos-in-tougher-hate-speech-policy/ (CNET)]

;International relations
*[[Taiwan–United States relations]], [[China–United States relations]], [[Cross-Strait relations]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] informs [[United States Congress|Congress]] of a potential $2 billion arms deal with [[Taiwan]] that includes the [[M1 Abrams|M1A2]], the U.S.'s latest [[main battle tank]], and a resupply of anti-air and anti-armor weapons. [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|China's foreign ministry]] says it is "severely concerned with" and "firmly against" the plan. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-06-05/trump-administration-readies-a-2-billion-taiwan-arms-package (Bloomberg)]

;Law and crime
*[[Australia]]n [[Australian Federal Police|federal police]] raid the headquarters of the country's public broadcaster, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]], regarding the alleged publication of classified material in a 2017 report on allegations that [[Australian Special forces]] engaged in unlawful killings and gross misconduct in [[Afghanistan]]. The day before, police raided ''[[Herald Sun]]'' journalist [[Annika Smethurst]]'s home regarding an alleged leak of national security information. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-48522729 (BBC News)] [https://www.businessinsider.com/australia-federal-police-raid-offices-australia-broadcasting-network-2019-6 (''Business Insider'')]
*[[Detroit Police Department|Detroit Police]] Chief [[James Craig (police chief)|James Craig]] announces the department is looking for a possible serial killer in three unsolved murders of [[sex worker]]s in the city dating back to March. [https://time.com/5602219/detroit-serial-killer-women/ (''Time'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Danish general election]]
**The center-left [[Social Democrats (Denmark)|Social Democrats]] win 48 of the 179 seats in the [[Folketing]] (parliament). Current Liberal Prime Minister [[Lars Løkke Rasmussen]] concedes defeat, paving the way for Social Democrat leader [[Mette Frederiksen]], who at 41 is set to be the country's youngest [[Prime Minister of Denmark|prime minister]]. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20190605/denmark-goes-to-the-polls-in-crucial-general-election-with-voters-seeking-change (''The Local'')] [https://euobserver.com/political/145099 (''EUobserver'')]
*[[President of Peru]] [[Martín Vizcarra]] wins a motion of confidence in the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress of the Republic]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-peru-politics/with-confidence-vote-peru-revives-debate-over-anti-graft-reforms-idUKKCN1T61WN (Reuters)]
